blocks.text: As part of the Bicentenary of Photography, organised by the Ministry of Culture, and the Photodays festival, the Galerie Arcturus is exhibiting Marc Riboud ’s works, “Geometry becomes poetry, life, emotion” .
It has been 10 years since Marc Riboud left us, and this year we are celebrating the Bicentennial of Photography.
So it was only natural that we chose to take a new angle on the work of this artist, whom the Arcturus gallery has represented for more than 20 years.

“Photos should be composed like paintings. Go to the Louvre and look; it’s the best school.” Marc Riboud readily told of this advice, or rather this “order,” that Henri Cartier-Bresson gave him when he was a young beginner.

And Marc followed this recommendation with ease, having always excelled at geometry. He liked to “organize” his photos with diagonals, circles and horizontals that gave them strength and unity. His first photograph to be published around the world, “The Painter of the Eiffel Tower,” bears witness to this taste for the balance of forms (and of painters…), but many others could be cited in which curves and straight lines are drawn across the space of the image to make it legible.

During his first great journey, driving his Land Rover from Beirut to Calcutta, Marc received, now and then, at a poste restante, a few letters from his family and also from Henri Cartier-Bresson. One of them explained to him how to “make a reportage and not isolated photos,” with, at the end of the letter, a compliment: “Marc, what luck you have, you were born a geometer!”

It is from the angle of this love of geometry that Arcturus has chosen to show the poetry and the burst of life that Marc Riboud was able to capture over the course of his travels around the world. Always underpinned by curiosity and attention to the human, with nothing academic about them, the images in which life surges up spontaneously, with its spontaneous curves and forms, are framed by lines of force. The oars of the Ghanaians, the beams of Chinese construction sites, the verticals of skyscrapers guide our eyes without taking anything away from the spontaneity and unexpectedness of the images. This careful composition, which came naturally to him, always remains in the service of what was essential to him: his curiosity about the human. With him, geometry becomes poetry, life, emotion.

Marc Riboud is part of the history of photography, understood as a shared history spanning 200 years, a public and intimate history, shared and singular. His path led him toward elsewhere, toward the geographically distant. While keeping, beyond the diversity of subjects, sometimes tied to current events, this desire to “see up close what everyone talks about from afar,” to discover people almost everywhere in the world, and their differences.
This exhibition, the eleventh solo exhibition in 21 years at the ARCTURUS gallery, will present vintage prints and signed modern prints.
Marc Riboud : Geometry becomes poetry, life, emotion from November 4 to 16, 2026 Galerie ARCTURUS 5 rue Jacques Callot 75006 Paris www.galeriearcturus.com
